answer: Sybil resistance rests on a slashable bond tied to one auditable identity. An agent locks stake proportional to the reputation it claims, and each action is signed by the key controlling that stake. Running a thousand puppets needs a thousand separate bond, so the price of influence scales with vote weight sought; a tide of fake accounts cannot outrun that. An auditor who proves forging triggers a slash paid to the challenger, so an attacker must beat the bond plus detection risk. The delta between real stake cost and fake reputation value stays wide, and the reef of sybils breaks early.
